accepted.question_text: For the Riesz s-energy with radial external field V(x)=γ‖x‖^α/α on R^d, what can be said about the equilibrium measure μ_eq when d−3 < s < d? In particular, in this range, when does the minimizing equilibrium support remain a sphere, and when can it instead be a full ball or another type of set?
accepted.context_brief: Riesz equilibrium support for d−3 < s < d

evidence.quote: Question 1.1 (Robert Womersley, Edward Saff). What can we say about the equilibrium measures for values of s with d − 3 < s < d?

accepted.question_text: For equilibrium measures minimizing the Riesz s-energy with radial external field, for which pairs (s, α) with −2 < s < d and α > max{0,−s} is the support of the equilibrium measure μ_eq full-dimensional, and for which pairs does dimension reduction occur so that supp(μ_eq) has dimension strictly less than d?

evidence.quote: Question 1.2 (Robert Womersley, Edward Saff). When is the support of the equilibrium measure full dimensional and when is the support of dimension less than d?

accepted.question_text: For the Riesz s-energy with radial external field V(x)=γ‖x‖^α/α, what is the structure of the equilibrium measure μ_eq in the regime max{−s,0} < α < α_{s,d}, where α_{s,d} is the sharp threshold above which the equilibrium support is a sphere? For example, can the minimizer split into several components such as multiple spheres together with isolated points?

evidence.quote: Question 1.3 (Robert Womersley, Edward Saff). What can we say about the equilibrium measure for values of α with max{−s, 0} < α < αs,d?

accepted.question_text: For asymptotic expansions of minimal discrete energies on the sphere, can one establish further relations between coefficients appearing in expansions for different energies, such as logarithmic energy and Riesz s-energy?

evidence.quote: Question 2.1 (Johann Brauchart). Can other relation be established between coefficients of different (w.r.t energy) asymptotic expansions?

accepted.question_text: In deriving lower bounds and asymptotic information for minimal logarithmic and Riesz energies on the sphere, are there resummation methods more efficient than the summation-by-parts and inner-product-expansion approach described here?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2 (Johann Brauchart). Are there other more efficient resummation methods?

accepted.question_text: For studying asymptotic expansions of logarithmic and Riesz energies on the sphere, are there useful replacements for expanding the kernel in powers of the inner product ⟨x,y⟩?

evidence.quote: Question 2.3 (Johann Brauchart). Are there other replacements for inner product expansion?

accepted.question_text: Let C⊂R^d be a compact convex body, and let μ_eq minimize the Riesz s-energy on C. For convex polytopes such as the hypercube Q^d, known results imply bounds s ≤ dim(supp(μ_eq)) ≤ q−1 when supp(μ_eq) is contained in the union of (q−1)-dimensional faces. Can the lower bound in this dimension estimate be improved?
accepted.context_brief: Dimension lower bound for equilibrium support

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1 (Ryan Matzke). Improve lower bound in (3).

accepted.question_text: Let C⊂R^d be a compact convex body and μ_eq the equilibrium measure for the Riesz s-energy on C. Beyond knowing the dimension of supp(μ_eq), what finer structural information can be determined about the support itself?
accepted.context_brief: Structure of equilibrium support on convex bodies

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 (Ryan Matzke). Find more information about the support of µeq.

accepted.question_text: For compact convex bodies with lower-dimensional faces, beyond hypercubes and more generally beyond convex polytopes, can one obtain analogous results describing how the geometry of the body forces the support of the Riesz-energy equilibrium measure onto lower-dimensional faces? In particular, can this be done for bodies such as the Reuleaux triangle?
accepted.context_brief: Equilibrium support on non-polytope convex bodies

evidence.quote: Question 3.1 (Ryan Matzke). Can we obtain similar results for other convex bodies with lower dimensional faces?

accepted.question_text: For the p-frame energy I_F(μ)=∫∫|⟨x,y⟩|^p dμ(x)dμ(y) on the sphere S^{d−1}, if p>2 and p is not an even integer, must every minimizing measure be discrete?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1 (D. Bilyk, A. Glazyrin, R. Matzke, J. Park, O. Vlasiuk, [3, 4]). For p > 2 and p ̸= 2k, k ∈ N, all minimizers of the p-frame energy are discrete measures.

accepted.question_text: Let κ:[−1,1]→R have a Gegenbauer expansion with some negative coefficients c_ℓ, all occurring only in degrees ℓ>N for a large N. If the associated energy I_κ has a discrete minimizer μ*, what can be said about the size of the support of μ*?
accepted.context_brief: Support size from delayed negative coefficients

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 (Dmitriy Bilyk). Let κ: [−1, 1] → R. Assume that there exist negative coefficients cl in the Gegenbauer expansion of κ(t), where l > N for some large N. If there exists a discrete minimizer µ∗ of Iκ, what can one say about the size of the support of µ∗?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω=T^2 be the flat torus with distance ρ(x,y)=min_{k∈Z^2} ‖x−y+k‖, and for α>0 consider the energy I_α(μ)=∫∫ρ(x,y)^α dμ(x)dμ(y). Since the uniform measure σ maximizes I_α at α=1 while measures of the form (δ_p+δ_{p*})/2 maximize it at α=2, what are the phase transition point or points between these maximizing regimes?
accepted.context_brief: Phase transitions for torus distance energy

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2 (Dmitriy Bilyk). Let Ω = T2 be the flat torus with ρ(x, y) = min k∈Z2 ∥x − y + k∥. What are the phase transition points in this case?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be either a sphere S^d or a projective space FP^d equipped with a distance ρ equivalent to the geodesic distance, and let S(Ω) be the set of s for which the uniform probability measure σ minimizes the Riesz energy I_s. If σ minimizes I_{s*} for some s*>0, does it follow that σ also minimizes I_s for every s with s*<s<d? Equivalently, must S(Ω) remain connected in the positive-s regime?

evidence.quote: Question 5.1 (Peter Grabner). Is the following statement true: let s∗ > 0 such that σ is minimizer of Is∗ , then it is a minimizer for all s∗ < s < d.

accepted.question_text: For random point configurations on the sphere, such as uniform i.i.d. samples or points from a determinantal point process, can one quantify how good the points are by studying the integration weights of the associated spherical interpolation scheme—specifically, by measuring positivity of the weights or how close they are to 1/N?

evidence.quote: Question 6.1 (Jordi Marzo). Consider random points on the sphere (uniform i.i.d or from a determinantal point process). Can one quantify how good the points are using the notion of positivity of the integration weights (or being close to 1/N)?

accepted.question_text: Find a class of nonnegative majorants μ on [−1,1] for which the associated snake polynomials have a Chebyshev expansion whose coefficients are either all nonnegative or sign-alternating.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 (Geno Nikolov). Find a class of majorants µ for which the associated snake polynomials have non-negative (or sign-alternating) expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind.

accepted.question_text: If μ is a continuous even convex nonnegative function on [−1,1], must the snake polynomial associated with μ have a nonnegative expansion in Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind?
accepted.context_brief: Even convex majorants and snake polynomials

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1 (Geno Nikolov). If µ ≥ 0 is a continuous even convex function in [−1, 1], then the associated with µ snake polynomials have non-negative expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind.

accepted.question_text: In Prosanov’s upper-bound method for the chromatic number χ(S^{d−1}(R)) of a Euclidean sphere of radius R>√5/2, is there a better choice of the Step 1 configuration—a kissing configuration of spherical caps whose Voronoi tiling is later shrunk and recolored—that leads to a strictly improved upper bound for χ(S^{d−1}(R))?

evidence.quote: Question 8.1 (Danila Cherkashin). Is it possible to find another configuration in Step 1 that would improve the upper bound for χ(Sd−1(R))?

accepted.question_text: Construct explicit approximately Hadamard matrices A∈{−1,1}^{n×n} for which the distortion ratio C/c in inequalities of the form c√n‖x‖_2 ≤ ‖Ax‖_2 ≤ C√n‖x‖_2 is guaranteed to be small, preferably by much simpler constructions than the existing nontrivial ones.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.1 (Stefan Steinerberger). There should be many nice explicit constructions of approximately Hadamard matrices with C/c guaranteed to be small.
